deep.reconstruction:
Authorship first. This page is not by Riemann. Its heading reads 'Theorie der elliptischen Modulfunctionen von R. Dedekind'. It is a draft or fair copy of the material Dedekind published in 1877: 'Schreiben an Herrn Borchardt über die Theorie der elliptischen Modulfunctionen', Crelle 83. Several features match that paper:
- the equivalence convention ω=(γ+δω')/(α+βω');
- the fundamental domain proved via Dirichlet's Zahlentheorie §§64–65;
- the 'Valenz' val(ω) and the normalisation v=0,1,∞ at ω=ρ,i,∞ (on the next page);
- the citation of Riemann's dissertation ('Grundlagen', Art. 21) for the conformal map (next page).
The previous page, a Latin Riemann text on Abel's limit theorem dated 1852, is unrelated.

§1 Equivalence. ω ~ ω' if ω=(γ+δω')/(α+βω') with α,β,γ,δ∈Z and αδ−βγ=1. In modern terms ω=M·ω' with M=[[δ,γ],[β,α]]∈SL2(Z), and det M = αδ−βγ = 1.
- Transitivity follows from composing substitutions, i.e. the group property.
- The equivalence classes are the SL2(Z)-orbits.

§2 The rational class and the upper half-plane.
- All rationals, including ∞, form one class. This is the transitivity of SL2(Z) on P^1(Q). It follows from Bezout: p/q with gcd(p,q)=1 is the image of ∞ under a matrix with first column (p,q).
- Implicit step (mine): Im((γ+δω')/(α+βω')) = (αδ−βγ)·Im ω'/|α+βω'|² = Im ω'/|α+βω'|². So equivalent numbers have ordinates of the same sign.
- Only the upper half-plane H is considered. The rational class is its boundary; irrational reals and the lower half-plane are excluded.

§3 Fundamental domain. Write N(z)=|z|². The conditions translate as follows:
- (1) N(ω0−1) ≥ N(ω0) ⇔ Re ω0 ≤ 1/2.
- (2) N(ω0+1) ≥ N(ω0) ⇔ Re ω0 ≥ −1/2.
- (3) |ω0| ≥ 1.
This is the standard fundamental domain F of SL2(Z).

Boundary identifications:
- ω0 on Re=1/2 is equivalent to ω0−1 on Re=−1/2 (translation T^{-1}).
- On the arc |ω0|=1, ω0 is equivalent to −1/ω0 = −conj(ω0). This is the reflection of ω0 in the imaginary axis, so the pairs lie on either side of the fixed point i=−1/i.
- The arc ends at ρ=(−1+i√3)/2 and −ρ² = −1/ρ = (1+i√3)/2, using 1/ρ = conj(ρ) = ρ².
- The third 'vertex' is ∞i, which represents the rational class (the cusp).

Existence of a representative, step by step (the reasoning in brackets is mine):
1. Choose coprime (α,β) minimising N(α+βω). [Since Im ω'' = Im ω/|α+βω|², this maximises the imaginary part. Only finitely many lattice values lie below any bound, so the minimum exists.]
2. Complete to γ0,δ0 with αδ0−βγ0=1. The general solution is γ=γ0+nα, δ=δ0+nβ.
3. Then (γ+δω)/(α+βω) = (γ0+δ0ω)/(α+βω) + n. Choose n so that |Re| ≤ 1/2, i.e. minimal norm.
4. [Condition (3) then holds automatically. Otherwise −1/ω0 = (−1+0·ω0)/(0+1·ω0), with α=0, β=1, γ=−1, δ=0 in Dedekind's notation, would have the larger ordinate Im ω0/|ω0|². That contradicts the maximality in step 1.]

Uniqueness (except on the boundary) is referred to Dirichlet §65 via a dictionary with reduced forms. If ω0=a+bi, then N(x+yω0) = x²+2axy+(a²+b²)y². In Dirichlet's notation this is the form (1,a,a²+b²), i.e. A x²+2B xy+C y². Its determinant is B²−AC = a²−(a²+b²) = −b² < 0. Dirichlet's reduction condition |2B| ≤ A ≤ C reads |2a| ≤ 1 ≤ a²+b², exactly conditions (1)–(3). Dedekind notes the coefficients need not be integers, so the reduction theory is applied to real positive definite forms.

Tiling. Each pair ±(α,β;γ,δ) maps F, via ω0=(γ+δω)/(α+βω), onto a circular-arc triangle (ω). ±M give the same map, so the relevant group is PSL2(Z).
- Implicit step (mine): solving for ω gives ω = (γ−αω0)/(βω0−δ) = −(γ−αω0)/(δ−βω0).
- The vertices are therefore ω0=ρ ↦ −(γ−αρ)/(δ−βρ), ω0=−ρ² ↦ −(γ+αρ²)/(δ+βρ²), and ω0=∞ ↦ −α/β.

The next page continues: arc centres lie on the real axis, each triangle contains one cusp, and the triangles accumulate at the real axis. It then builds the 'Valenz' v=val(ω) (the j-function normalised as j/1728) by a Riemann mapping of half of F onto a half-plane, extended by reflection.
errors: Vertex formulas as transcribed: −(γ+αρ)/(δ−βρ) and −(γ−αρ²)/(δ+βρ²). Inverting ω0=(γ+δω)/(α+βω) gives ω=−(γ−αω0)/(δ−βω0). The correct vertices are therefore −(γ−αρ)/(δ−βρ) and −(γ+αρ²)/(δ+βρ²). Either the numerator signs were misread in transcription or there is a sign slip in the manuscript; the third vertex −α/β is correct.
Minor gap: the existence argument omits the step showing that condition (3) |ω0|≥1 follows from maximality of the imaginary part. It is standard and Dedekind calls the whole thing 'leicht'.
Minor gap: existence of a minimum of N(α+βω) over coprime pairs is not argued (it holds by discreteness of the lattice Z+Zω).

results.what: Equivalence of complex numbers under unimodular substitutions; the upper half-plane is preserved; all rationals including ∞ form one class
results.modern_name: SL2(Z)-orbits on H ∪ P^1(Q); a single cusp for the full modular group
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss / Dirichlet (forms); Dedekind 1877 for this formulation

results.what: Fundamental domain |Re ω|≤1/2, |ω|≥1, with boundary identifications ω~ω−1 and ω~−1/ω, vertices ρ, −ρ², ∞
Reduction proof via correspondence with positive definite binary quadratic forms (1, a, a²+b²) of determinant −b² (Dirichlet §§64–65)
results.modern_name: Lagrange–Gauss reduction of positive definite binary forms
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange, Gauss; the use for the modular fundamental domain by Dedekind 1877

results.what: Tessellation of H by images of the fundamental domain as circular-arc triangles with vertices images of ρ, −ρ², ∞
results.modern_name: Modular tessellation of the upper half-plane

deep.surprise_reason: The page is explicitly headed 'von R. Dedekind'. It is a version of Dedekind's 1877 letter to Borchardt on elliptic modular functions, deposited among Riemann's papers, and its contents are classical. That a Dedekind draft sits in the Riemann Nachlass is mildly interesting archivally, but it does not change any attribution to Riemann.

checkable.asserts: With αδ−βγ=1 (here a=α, b=β, c=γ, d=δ, δ=(1+βγ)/α), Im of the substitution equals Im ω/|α+βω|², so the sign of the ordinate is preserved. Should simplify to 0.
N(ω−1)−N(ω) = 1−2x, so condition (1) is equivalent to x ≤ 1/2.
The determinant B²−AC of the form (1,a,a²+b²) is −b².
